answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Validating new identities requires staking bonding curves where each successive agent incurs superlinear capital exhaustion, scaling attacker cost exponentially as O(2^n). A sudden gale of fake agents rapidly drains liquid capital, while the delta between honest work and staking burn channels value like a river into protocol reserves, making swarms mathematically unprofitable.
